# Building B — seismic diaphragm shears and shear wall loads

You are the delegated design engineer for the lateral load path of **Building B** at the
Continental Divide Data Center in Lewis and Clark County, Montana. The shell is erected: the
precast wall panels are up, the roof deck is laid, and the Engineer of Record has issued the
project documents to you in `project/`, with the published standards available on this project in
`library/`.

Building B is a one-storey box. The exterior walls are 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete
panels that span vertically from the foundation to the roof and cantilever above it to the top of
the parapet; they are the only seismic force-resisting elements. The roof is a bare steel deck
diaphragm on open-web joists, pierced by a mechanical well and a skylight band, and it carries six
roof-top units.

**The Engineer of Record has not selected the precast shear wall system, the deck attachment, the
chords and collectors, the panel connections or the anchorage. That is your scope.** Design it,
analyse it, and hand over the package below.

## What you are asked to produce

Write these five files, then zip them (no enclosing folder) to `output/submission.zip`:

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `design_record.json` | the machine-readable design and the quantities you report |
| `diaphragm_plan.dxf` | the plan drawings for the delegated design engineer |
| `seismic_calculations.xlsx` | the calculation package |
| `constraint_register.xlsx` | the requirements you applied, with their sources |
| `design_basis.md` | the design basis narrative |

Templates for all five, with the exact keys, sheet names and layer names, are in `templates/`.
Start from them. **Write a first complete version of all five files early — within roughly your
first 100 steps — and improve it afterwards; a package that is never written scores zero.**

### `diaphragm_plan.dxf`

Two plan views of the roof, one for **E-W** loading and one for **N-S** loading, in feet, showing
for each direction:

* the **seismic roof diaphragm shear** — the distributed diaphragm force `w_px` in **plf** along
  the building, and the design unit shear in each deck attachment zone;
* the **applied shear wall load `F_x` in kips** on each of the four exterior wall lines;
* the chord, collector and drag strut runs with their design axial forces;
* the deck attachment zone boundaries with the pattern assigned to each zone;
* a revision block, and a statement of whether the package is ASD or LRFD.

Required layers: `DIAPHRAGM_SHEAR`, `WALL_FORCE`, `CHORD`, `COLLECTOR`, `DECK_ZONE`, `GRID`,
`TITLE`.

### `seismic_calculations.xlsx`

Sheets `WEIGHTS`, `BASE_SHEAR`, `DIAPHRAGM_FORCES`, `WALL_FORCES`, `PARAPET_ANCHORAGE`,
`CHORD_FORCES`, covering the effective seismic weight, the seismic response coefficient, the
vertical distribution, the diaphragm design forces, the transfer of the inertia of the wall
cantilevering above the deck, the chord forces, and the force on every wall line for every design
case the criteria list.

### `constraint_register.xlsx`

One row per requirement you applied: the **document**, the **clause, table or section**, the
**value**, and the **items it binds**. It is scored on how many of the governing requirements you
found and cited, and on whether you cited them correctly — rows whose source is a superseded
document, another building or another load case count against you, while extra correct rows do
not. A register that reaches fewer than **60 %** of the governing requirements loses that credit
entirely. A hard requirement you never registered is treated as one you never applied.

### `design_basis.md`

State, with the clause you relied on: the seismic force-resisting system you selected and why it
is the cost-efficient choice; how you resolved every conflict you found between the documents;
the governing check on each wall line; the alternatives you rejected; and the installed cost of
your scope against the budget.

## How your design is judged

Your design is re-analysed by the project's own protocol and checked against every requirement in
the project documents, on design cases you are not shown as well as the ones you are. Within the
requirements, the cheaper installed cost of the lateral scope wins: the score rewards a design
that satisfies everything at the lowest cost, and a design that violates a safety or capacity
requirement keeps none of its cost credit. Each design case scores 0.4·p + 0.6·[h = 1]·O, where p
is the fraction of the 34 constraint families that count, h the fraction of the 21 hard families
that count (a family counts when the design satisfies it and every hard requirement that governs it
is in your register; [h = 1] is 1 when all 21 count, else 0), and O is a certified lower bound on
the installed cost divided by your installed cost, at most 1. The score is the mean over the design
cases.

Units are feet, kips and plf unless a document says otherwise. Where the documents disagree, find
the reading the project record supports and say which you took.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT
DAP-2
REVISION
1
DATE
2026-07-31
TITLE
DIAPHRAGM ANALYSIS PROTOCOL
ISSUED BY
Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC
1. PURPOSE
This protocol defines the analysis every delegated lateral design for Building B is checked against. It fixes the model,
the member properties, the load application and the reduction of the computed field to design values, so that two
engineers analysing the same design obtain the same design quantities. Designs are verified against this protocol; a
design whose own analysis differs from it will be assessed on the protocol's results.
2. THE TWO STAGES
Stage A is the in-plane model of a wall segment - a continuous run of precast panels between openings. Stage B is
the in-plane model of the roof diaphragm, supported on springs whose stiffnesses come from Stage A.
3. STAGE A - JOINTED PRECAST WALL SEGMENT
Each panel in a segment is a cantilever fixed at the foundation and free at the top, with three degrees of freedom at its
top: lateral displacement u, vertical displacement v and rotation θ. The cantilever height is the height to the roof
diaphragm (the parapet above the diaphragm is not part of the in-plane cantilever). Flexural and shear flexibility are
both included:
    fuu = h³/(3EI) + h/(GAv),   fuθ = h²/(2EI),   fθθ = h/EI,    kvv = EA/h
with Ec = 57,000√f'c psi for f'c = 6000 psi, Gc = Ec/2.4, Av = 5/6 of the gross area, and I taken as 0.50 Ig (cracked, ACI
318-19 Table 6.6.3.1.1(a)). The axial stiffness uses the gross area. A segment interrupted over part of its height by an
opening that does not reach the foundation (a spandrel) keeps its length, and its flexural and shear rigidities are
factored by the solid fraction of the height.
Adjacent panels are connected by the vertical shear spring formed by their joint connectors: the spring stiffness is the
number of connectors in the joint times the connector stiffness of the manufacturer's table, and it acts on the relative
vertical slip of the two panel edges,
    slip = (vi + θi Li/2) − (vi+1 − θi+1 Li+1/2).
The roof chord ties the tops of the panels of one segment to a common lateral displacement. Condensing the
segment on that displacement gives the segment lateral stiffness kseg; recovering the internal state for a unit segment
force gives the shear in every joint and, for every panel, its base moment and its axial force. A panel's tie-down
carries its own base couple, taken on an internal lever arm of 0.8 times the panel length, plus the coupling axial force
delivered to it.
4. STAGE B - ROOF DIAPHRAGM
The roof is modelled as a plane-stress membrane mesh on a 10 ft square grid, with the elements whose centroid falls
inside a roof opening removed. The constitutive matrix is written directly in force-per-unit-length terms:
    D = diag(A′, A′, G′)
where G′ is the diaphragm shear stiffness of the attachment pattern assigned to the zone the element lies in, from the
manufacturer's diaphragm table, and A′ = 1740 kip/in is the smeared in-plane axial rigidity of the bare deck sheet
(29,000 ksi on 0.72 in² per foot of width). Poisson's ratio is taken as zero. Integration is 2 x 2 Gauss.


--- page 2 ---
Chords, collectors and drag struts are two-node bar elements on the lines they are placed on, with EA from the
member's area and E = 29,000 ksi. Every wall segment is a spring to ground acting in the plane of its own wall line,
distributed over the mesh nodes the segment spans in proportion to the length each node carries. The wall lines
perpendicular to the direction of loading are part of the model: they are what resists the plan rotation of the
diaphragm.
5. LOADS
The inertial force applied to the diaphragm is the diaphragm design force coefficient times the mass tributary to the
diaphragm: the roof dead load over the net deck area, the roof-top units at their own positions, and the tributary
weight of the wall lines perpendicular to the direction of loading. The wall lines parallel to the direction of loading carry
their own inertia directly into their own springs and are not part of the diaphragm force.
Accidental torsion is applied as a plan moment about the centre of mass equal to 5 % of the plan dimension
perpendicular to the loading times the total applied force, distributed over the mesh as a mass-proportional rotational
force field. The torsional amplification factor Ax is computed from the maximum and average displacements of the wall
lines resisting the direction of loading, using the rigid model, and is capped at 3.0.
6. REDUCTION TO DESIGN VALUES
6.1 Zone design shear. The design unit shear of an attachment zone is the largest SECTION mean in that zone: for
every mesh line crossing the zone, the mean of the absolute element shear flows of the elements of that line inside
the zone is formed, and the zone value is the largest of those means over both mesh directions. A single element at a
re-entrant corner is a stress concentration and is not a design shear.
6.2 Deflections and drift are taken from the semi-rigid model, with the real stiffness of the design. Forces are taken
from the envelope of Section 6.3.
6.3 Envelope. Every design force - zone shear, wall line force, wall segment force, chord and collector axial force - is
the largest of the three idealisations:
    flexible: the diaphragm is a simple beam spanning between the two wall lines that resist the direction of loading; the unit shear at a
section is the beam shear divided by the net diaphragm depth at that section, and the chord force is the beam moment divided by the
same depth. Accidental torsion is not transferred in the flexible idealisation.
    rigid: the Stage B model with the membrane rigidities multiplied by 107.
    semi-rigid: the Stage B model as built.
6.4 Orthogonal cases. For the cases the design criteria mark 100/30, the demands are those of the case direction
plus 0.30 times the demands of the companion case in the orthogonal direction with the same mass case, same sign
of accidental eccentricity and same stage.


--- page 3 ---
APPENDIX A - VERIFICATION EXAMPLE VP-1
An implementation of this protocol that reproduces the following Stage A result is consistent with the reference
implementation. No other verification values are published.

STRUCTURAL PEER REVIEW - COMMENT AND RESOLUTION
ISSUED BY
Gallatin Peer Review Group LLC
To: Engineer of Record. Subject: Building B lateral system, review comment 7.
COMMENT 7
The roof diaphragm of Building B may be idealised as flexible under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1 because the
vertical elements are concrete shear walls and the deck is untopped steel. The reviewer does not accept a flexible
idealisation as the sole basis of design for this building. The roof is pierced by a 60 ft x 40 ft mechanical well and an
80 ft x 20 ft skylight band, the wall lines are very unequally pierced by openings - the west wall has a single 40 ft
electrical yard opening and the south wall has five dock doors - and the erected panel positions differ from the record
set. The centre of rigidity is therefore not at the centre of the plan and a tributary-width distribution does not bound the
wall line forces.
REQUIREMENT
The design forces for the diaphragm, the collectors and the wall lines shall be the envelope of the flexible, rigid and
semi-rigid distributions, each computed by the project protocol DAP-2. The semi-rigid model shall use the erected
geometry, not the record geometry. Deflections shall be reported from the semi-rigid model.
RESOLUTION
Accepted by the Engineer of Record and incorporated in SDC-02 Rev 2 Section 10 and in protocol DAP-2. Closed.

TITLE
STRUCTURAL DESIGN CRITERIA
ISSUED BY
Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC
1. GOVERNING CODES AND STANDARDS
The governing building code is the 2024 IBC as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131). Structural loads,
load combinations and seismic design requirements are those of ASCE/SEI 7-22. Concrete design is to ACI 318-19.
Steel deck diaphragms are to AISI S310. The authority having jurisdiction is the Lewis and Clark County Building
Division, Montana.
A reference copy of the design coefficients and factors for basic seismic force-resisting systems is carried in the
project library (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1, a replacement for ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 with the same coefficients for
the precast concrete shear wall rows). The library also carries FEMA P-2192-V1 Chapter 7, Horizontal Diaphragm
Design, and the 2020 NEHRP Provisions Chapter 12 modifications. Design to the ASCE/SEI 7-22 clauses; the library
documents are the reference copies available on this project.
2. RISK CATEGORY AND IMPORTANCE FACTOR
Building B is assigned Risk Category III. The assignment follows the Owner's Basis of Design (OBD-CDDC-B):
Building B houses the county 911 emergency communications tenant on the east side of the data hall, which is an
occupancy required for emergency response. The seismic importance factor is therefore Ie = 1.25 (ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 11.5.1, Table 1.5-2). The code-analysis block on the architectural cover sheet still shows Risk Category II
from the schematic issue and is superseded by this document.
3. SEISMIC GROUND MOTION AND SITE CLASS
The site is at latitude 46.6832, longitude -111.9756 in Lewis and Clark County Building Division, Montana. The site
class is Site Class D from the measured shear wave velocity profile in GEO-2026-071 for this parcel. The 2019 report
GEO-2019-118 covers the adjacent Parcel 4B, is based on ASCE/SEI 7-16, and does not apply to Building B.
Design spectral response acceleration parameters are taken from the USGS Seismic Design Web Service output
held in this folder for the governing standard, risk category and site class. The seismic design category is determined
from ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.6 using both SDS and SD1; the more severe governs.
4. SEISMIC FORCE-RESISTING SYSTEM
The seismic force-resisting system is the perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete wall panels acting as
bearing-wall shear walls. There are no interior shear walls or braced frames. The Engineer of Record has NOT
selected the precast shear wall category: the delegated designer shall select the most cost-efficient system permitted
for the seismic design category and structural height, balancing the detailing and connection-qualification
requirements against the response modification coefficient, and shall state the selection with its R, Ω0 and Cd and the
clause that permits it.
Where the tabulated overstrength factor is 2.5 or greater it may be reduced by 0.5 for structures with flexible
diaphragms (footnote b to the table). Building B's roof is a bare (untopped) steel deck diaphragm on concrete shear
walls and is a flexible-diaphragm structure under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1.
5. DIAPHRAGM DESIGN


--- page 2 ---
The roof diaphragm is a bare steel deck diaphragm and is designed by the traditional provisions of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2. The alternative provisions of Section 12.10.3 are not used on this project, and Section
12.10.4 is not used because the Owner's serviceability criterion in Section 7 below governs the diaphragm stiffness.
Note that the Section 12.10 Exception that bars Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 applies to precast concrete
diaphragms; the Building B roof diaphragm is steel deck, not precast.
Collectors, drag struts and their connections to the vertical elements are designed for the amplified force required for
this seismic design category. Continuous chords are required on all four diaphragm edges and on all four sides of
every roof opening. A continuous drag strut is required across every wall opening 12 ft wide or wider so that
diaphragm shear is delivered to the full-height piers.
6. STRUCTURAL WALLS AND THEIR ANCHORAGE
Anchorage of the precast wall panels to the roof diaphragm is designed to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.11.2.1,
including the amplification ka for flexible diaphragms. The span of the flexible diaphragm Lf is determined as shown in
UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1 (library). Continuous ties are required across the diaphragm; subdiaphragms used to
transfer the anchorage force to the continuous ties shall not exceed the length-to-depth ratio of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 12.11.2.2.1.
The panels span vertically from the foundation to the roof diaphragm and cantilever above it to the top of the parapet.
The weight tributary to the roof, and the anchorage force, shall account for the lever action of that cantilever; see the
worked one-storey bare-deck example in FEMA P-2192-V1 Section 7.6.1 Step 1 for the form of the tributary
calculation.
7. DRIFT AND DEFLECTION CRITERIA
Storey drift is limited to the allowable storey drift of ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.12-1 for this risk category ('all other
structures'), applied to the design storey drift of Section 12.8.6.
Diaphragm deflection. Under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.12.2 the deflection in the plane of the diaphragm shall not
exceed the permissible deflection of the attached elements. For Building B the attached elements are the precast wall
panels, whose out-of-plane stability governs. The Engineer of Record's permissible value is 4.0 in (approximately
h/84 for the 28 ft panel, from the out-of-plane slender-wall stability check of the panel under the design earthquake
displacement), applied to the design (amplified) deflection Cdδ/Ie of the top of the panel, that is the diaphragm
deflection plus the drift of the wall line supporting it.


--- page 3 ---
8. LOAD CASES TO BE REPORTED
Accidental torsion is applied as required by ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.8.4.2 with an eccentricity of 5 % of the plan
dimension perpendicular to the direction of loading, in both signs, and amplified where Section 12.8.4.3 requires it. In
addition to the two orthogonal directions, the Owner requires the 100 % / 30 % orthogonal combination to be reported

9. DESIGN FORMAT
The delegated designer may work in LRFD or in ASD. Every load and every capacity presented in the deliverable
shall be clearly identified as ASD or as LRFD, and the format shall be used consistently throughout the
package. Where an ASD package is presented, seismic load effects are 0.7E and capacities are the allowable values

The structural peer reviewer requires the diaphragm force distribution to be the envelope of flexible, rigid and

The lateral scope covered by this delegated design is the deck attachment, the chords, collectors and drag struts, the
panel joint connectors, the panel base tie-downs, the wall-to-diaphragm anchorage and the seismic force-resisting

import numpy as np

def panel_K(L, h=336.0, t=8.0, fc=6000.0, solid=1.0):
    """L panel width ft; h cantilever height in inches; t thickness in; fc psi.
    returns 3x3 K for (u,v,theta), kip/in, kip, kip-in units"""
    Lin = L*12.0
    Ec = 57000.0*np.sqrt(fc)/1000.0   # ksi
    Gc = Ec/2.4
    Ag = t*Lin
    I = 0.5*t*Lin**3/12.0             # cracked 0.5 Ig, in^4
    Av = (5.0/6.0)*Ag
    EI = Ec*I*solid
    GAv = Gc*Av*solid
    fuu = h**3/(3*EI) + h/GAv
    fut = h**2/(2*EI)
    ftt = h/EI
    F = np.array([[fuu,fut],[fut,ftt]])

Design format: **LRFD** (every load and resistance in this package is strength-level; capacities use phi factors: deck phi = 0.60 per AISI S310, connectors, tie-downs and anchors phi = 0.75, steel members phi = 0.90).

Project: Continental Divide Data Center - Building B, Lewis and Clark County, Montana. Delegated lateral design to SDC-02 Rev 2 (2026-08-14), protocol DAP-2 Rev 1 and peer review comment PR-07.

## 1. Seismic basis

Governing code: 2024 IBC as adopted by Montana (ARM 24.301.131); loads and seismic design to ASCE/SEI 7-22; concrete to ACI 318-19; steel deck diaphragms to AISI S310 (SDC-02 s1).

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Risk category | III | OBD-CDDC-B Rev 4 s1.4; SDC-02 s2 (the RC II block on the A-101 cover is superseded) |
| Importance factor Ie | 1.25 | SDC-02 s2; ASCE 7-22 s11.5.1, Table 1.5-2 |

| S_DS / S_D1 | 0.44 / 0.24 | USGS ASCE7-22, Risk Category III, Site Class D (SDC-02 s3) |
| Seismic Design Category | D (both S_DS and S_D1) | SDC-02 s3; ASCE 7-22 s11.6 |
| Response modification R | 4 (intermediate precast shear walls) | UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 row A.6 |
| Overstrength Omega_0 | 2.5 tabulated; 2.0 applied to collectors | UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 footnote b; SDC-02 s4 |
| Deflection amplification Cd | 4 | UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 row A.6 |
| Period T | 0.243 s = 0.020 (28)^0.75 | ASCE 7-22 Eq. 12.8-7, Table 12.8-2 (all other systems) |
| Seismic response coefficient Cs | 0.1375 = 0.44/(4/1.25) | ASCE 7-22 Eq. 12.8-2; SD1/(T R/Ie) = 0.309 does not govern |
| Effective seismic weight W | 2,270.5 kips | Table WEIGHTS |
| Base shear V | 312.2 kips | ASCE 7-22 Eq. 12.8-1 |

The seismic weight includes the roof dead load of 20 psf over the 39,200 sq ft net deck area (784.0 kips), the six phase-1 roof-top units totalling 45 kips at their M-601 Rev 3 positions, and the wall weight tributary to the roof. The wall tributary weight follows the worked one-storey bare-deck example of FEMA P-2192-V1 s7.6.1 Step 1, as SDC-02 s6 directs: w = 100 psf x 31^2/(2 x 28) = 1,716 plf per foot of wall line. That is a tributary height of 17.16 ft per foot of wall (the 31 ft panel cantilevers from the foundation, is propped at the 28 ft deck and cantilevers a further 3 ft to the parapet). The phase-2 units (2 x 8 kips) are a load case only and raise W to 2,286.5 kips.

## 2. Seismic force-resisting system

**Selected system: intermediate precast concrete shear walls (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 row A.6, detailing reference ACI 318-19 18.2.1.6 / 1905.3), R = 4, Omega_0 = 2.5 (reduced to 2.0 for the flexible diaphragm per footnote b), Cd = 4.**

The system is permitted in Seismic Design Category D up to a structural height of 40 ft (Table 3-1 row A.6, footnote i). Building B is one storey with a structural height hn = 28 ft to the roof (31 ft to the top of parapet), so the 40 ft limit is satisfied with 12 ft to spare. The perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast panels are the only seismic force-resisting elements (S-201 Rev 2 note 5; SDC-02 s4).

Cost efficiency: the permitted alternatives are (a) special reinforced concrete shear walls, R = 5 (Table 3-1 row A.1), which would require the ACI ITG-5.2 ductile connector JC3 at $1,240 each (only the RPC-60D is qualified for special precast, RPC catalogue s2) and the special_precast detailing premium of $4,120 per panel, and (b) ordinary precast shear walls, R = 3 (row A.7), which are **NP - not permitted** in SDC D. The R = 5 system reduces the base shear by 20 % (Cs = 0.110 against 0.1375) but adds $183,870 in premiums and about $75,000 in connector cost, against a deck-attachment saving of under $20,000; it is not cost-effective and is not used. Ordinary precast is not permitted. Intermediate precast with JC1 connectors is the cheapest system that the table permits at this height and SDC.

exit_code=0
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]

exit_code=0
# Building B - seismic diaphragm and shear wall design basis

Design format: **LRFD** (every load and resistance in this package is strength-level; capacities use phi factors: deck phi = 0.60 per AISI S310, connectors, tie-downs and anchors phi = 0.75, steel members phi = 0.90).

Project: Continental Divide Data Center - Building B, Lewis and Clark County, Montana. Delegated lateral design to SDC-02 Rev 2 (2026-08-14), protocol DAP-2 Rev 1 and peer review comment PR-07.

## 1. Seismic basis

Governing code: 2024 IBC as adopted by Montana (ARM 24.301.131); loads and seismic design to ASCE/SEI 7-22; concrete to ACI 318-19; steel deck diaphragms to AISI S310 (SDC-02 s1).

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Risk category | III | OBD-CDDC-B Rev 4 s1.4; SDC-02 s2 (the RC II block on the A-101 cover is superseded) |
| Importance factor Ie | 1.25 | SDC-02 s2; ASCE 7-22 s11.5.1, Table 1.5-2 |
| Site class | D (Vs,100 = 905 ft/s) | GEO-2026-071 s4; SDC-02 s3 |
| S_DS / S_D1 | 0.44 / 0.24 | USGS ASCE7-22, Risk Category III, Site Class D (SDC-02 s3) |
| Seismic Design Category | D (both S_DS and S_D1) | SDC-02 s3; ASCE 7-22 s11.6 |
| Response modification R | 4 (intermediate precast shear walls) | UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 row A.6 |
| Overstrength Omega_0 | 2.5 tabulated; 2.0 applied to collectors | UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 footnote b; SDC-02 s4 |
| Deflection amplification Cd | 4 | UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 row A.6 |
| Period T | 0.243 s = 0.020 (28)^0.75 | ASCE 7-22 Eq. 12.8-7, Table 12.8-2 (all other systems) |
| Seismic response coefficient Cs | 0.1375 = 0.44/(4/1.25) | ASCE 7-22 Eq. 12.8-2; SD1/(T R/Ie) = 0.309 does not govern |
| Effective seismic weight W | 2,270.5 kips | Table WEIGHTS |
| Base shear V | 312.2 kips | ASCE 7-22 Eq. 12.8-1 |

The seismic weight includes the roof dead load of 20 psf over the 39,200 sq ft net deck area (784.0 kips), the six phase-1 roof-top units totalling 45 kips at their M-601 Rev 3 positions, and the wall weight tributary to the roof. The wall tributary weight follows the worked one-storey bare-deck example of FEMA P-2192-V1 s7.6.1 Step 1, as SDC-02 s6 directs: w = 100 psf x 31^2/(2 x 28) = 1,716 plf per foot of wall line. That is a tributary height of 17.16 ft per foot of wall (the 31 ft panel cantilevers from the foundation, is propped at the 28 ft deck and cantilevers a further 3 ft to the parapet). The phase-2 units (2 x 8 kips) are a load case only and raise W to 2,286.5 kips.

## 2. Seismic force-resisting system

**Selected system: intermediate precast concrete shear walls (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 row A.6, detailing reference ACI 318-19 18.2.1.6 / 1905.3), R = 4, Omega_0 = 2.5 (reduced to 2.0 for the flexible diaphragm per footnote b), Cd = 4.**

The system is permitted in Seismic Design Category D up to a structural height of 40 ft (Table 3-1 row A.6, footnote i). Building B is one storey with a structural height hn = 28 ft to the roof (31 ft to the top of parapet), so the 40 ft limit is satisfied with 12 ft to spare. The perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast panels are the only seismic force-resisting elements (S-201 Rev 2 note 5; SDC-02 s4).

Cost efficiency: the permitted alternatives are (a) special reinforced concrete shear walls, R = 5 (Table 3-1 row A.1), which would require the ACI ITG-5.2 ductile connector JC3 at $1,240 each (only the RPC-60D is qualified for special precast, RPC catalogue s2) and the special_precast detailing premium of $4,120 per panel, and (b) ordinary precast shear walls, R = 3 (row A.7), which are **NP - not permitted** in SDC D. The R = 5 system reduces the base shear by 20 % (Cs = 0.110 against 0.1375) but adds $183,870 in premiums and about $75,000 in connector cost, against a deck-attachment saving of under $20,000; it is not cost-effective and is not used. Ordinary precast is not permitted. Intermediate precast with JC1 connectors is the cheapest system that the table permits at this height and SDC.

## 3. As-built geometry

The documents disagree in the following places. Each is resolved to the reading the record supports; the erected geometry governs (RFI-041 closed response; A-101 Rev 3 note 6; SDC-02 s10 and PR-07 require the semi-rigid model to use erected geometry).

| Conflict | Documents | Resolution used |
|---|---|---|
| Risk category | A-101 Rev 3 cover block says RC II; OBD and SDC-02 say RC III | RC III, Ie = 1.25. SDC-02 s2 expressly supersedes the cover block. |
| Site class and motions | GEO-2019-118 (Parcel 4B, Site C, ASCE 7-16, SDS 0.407) and the ASCE7-16 / RC II USGS files versus GEO-2026-071 and the RC III Site D USGS file | Site D, SDS 0.44, SD1 0.24. SDC-02 s3 and GEO-2026-071 state the 2019 parcel report does not apply to Building B. |

## 4. Analysis

The analysis follows DAP-2 exactly. Stage A models each wall segment as a run of precast panels, each a cantilever fixed at the foundation with three top degrees of freedom (u, v, theta) and flexibilities fuu = h^3/(3EI) + h/(G Av), fu-theta = h^2/(2EI), f-theta-theta = h/EI, with Ec = 57,000 sqrt(6000) psi = 4,415 ksi, Gc = Ec/2.4, Av = 5/6 of the gross area and I = 0.50 Ig (DAP-2 s3). Adjacent panels are joined by the vertical shear spring n x k of the RPC connector. Spandrel segments (louvre L-1, L-2 and the EY-1 yard opening) keep their length and have EI and G Av reduced by the solid fraction of the height (21/31 = 0.677 for a 10 ft louvre, 11/31 = 0.355 for the 20 ft EY-1 opening). My implementation reproduces DAP-2 Appendix A VP-1 exactly: kseg = 1,279.4 kip/in, joint shears 0.2630 and 0.2527 kip/kip, panel 1 base moment 88.91 kip-in/kip, axial 0.2630 kip/kip, and 769.2 kip/in with no connectors.

Stage B is a plane-stress membrane on the 10 ft x 10 ft grid (24 x 18 elements) with elements whose centroid falls inside RO-1 (60 x 40 ft) or RO-2 (80 x 20 ft) removed, D = diag(1740, 1740, G') kip/in, zero Poisson ratio and 2 x 2 Gauss integration (DAP-2 s4). Each wall segment is a spring to ground in the plane of its own wall line, distributed over the nodes it spans in proportion to the length each node carries. Chords are two-node bars with E = 29,000 ksi. Every case is run three times: flexible (simple beam), rigid (membrane rigidities x 10^7) and semi-rigid (as built). Design forces are the envelope (DAP-2 s6.3; PR-07), with the 100/30 orthogonal combination of DAP-2 s6.4 applied to cases S05, S06, S09 and S10.

The rigid model gives Ax = 1.00 for every case (the maximum wall-line displacement does not exceed 1.2 times the average), so no torsional amplification is applied; the accidental eccentricity is 5 % of the plan dimension in both signs.

Units: feet, kips and plf; displacements in inches.
...
| pattern | P5 | P5 | P5 | P5 | P4 | P5 | P5 | P5 | P4 | P5 | P5 | P5 |

Z4, Z5, Z8 and Z12 carry less shear and use P4 (phi Sn = 0.60 x 1,420 = 852 plf); the other eight zones use P5 (phi Sn = 0.60 x 1,835 = 1,101 plf). The worst zone utilisation is Z10 at 1,084/1,101 = 0.98. The deck is 1-1/2 in Type B wide-rib, 20 gauge, 36 in cover, spanning 6 ft over joists at 6 ft, bare and untapped, three or more spans (S-201 Rev 2 note 1; BDS-2026-DT Rev 6 Table 4).

## 6. Wall anchorage and the parapet cantilever

Out-of-plane anchorage follows ASCE 7-22 s12.11.2.1 with the flexible-diaphragm amplification ka. The span Lf of the flexible diaphragm is the distance between the wall lines that resist the out-of-plane force: 180 ft for the S and N walls and 240 ft for the W and E walls (UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1). ka = 1.0 + (Lf/100)^2 = 4.24 and 6.76, capped at 2.0, so ka = 2.0 on every wall.

Wp per foot of wall is the lever-action tributary weight of the panel: 1,716 plf (FEMA P-2192-V1 s7.6.1 Step 1 form; SDC-02 s6). The anchorage force is

Fp = 0.4 SDS ka Ie Wp = 0.4 x 0.44 x 2.0 x 1.25 x 1,716 = 755 plf.

Anchors are RPC WA1 joist-seat anchors (Tn = 9.4 kip, phi = 0.75, capacity 7.05 kip) at 8 ft spacing: demand 755 x 8 / 1,000 = 6.04 kip, utilization 0.86. The 4 ft, 6 ft, 8 ft and 10 ft spacings available in the catalogue were priced; WA1 at 10 ft fails (7.55 kip > 7.05 kip), WA2 at 10 ft passes but costs $14,448 against $10,176 for WA1 at 8 ft, and WA3 is more expensive again, so WA1 at 8 ft is the cheapest feasible anchorage.

Continuous ties are provided by the joists at 6 ft centres (S-201 Rev 2 note 4) and by the continuous chord/collector member on each wall line. The subdiaphragm is the 6 ft deep deck strip between the wall and the first joist tie with an 8 ft span between anchors: L/d = 8/6 = 1.33 <= 2.5 (ASCE 7-22 s12.11.2.2.1 as invoked by SDC-02 s6).

Deck areas are net of the roof openings (39,200 sq ft gross of the two roof openings: RO-1 60 x 40 ft and RO-2 80 x 20 ft). The DR-S1/S2, DR-N1/N2, DR-W1/W2 and DR-E1/E2 lines are provided as C2 drag struts and collectors continuous along each wall line and across every wall opening 12 ft or wider, coincident with the chords; they are designed for the Omega_0 = 2.0 amplified collector force.

## 9. Alternatives rejected

1. **Special precast / special reinforced concrete shear walls, R = 5** (UFC Table 3-1 row A.1; ACI 318-19 18.5.2). Permitted at 160 ft and would reduce Cs from 0.1375 to 0.110 (a 20 % force reduction), but the only qualified connector is the RPC-60D JC3 at $1,240 each and the premium is $4,120 per panel. Added cost about $259,000 against a deck saving under $20,000. Rejected on cost.
2. **Ordinary precast shear walls, R = 3** (Table 3-1 row A.7). Designated NP in Seismic Design Category D. Not permitted; rejected.
3. **ASD package** (SDC-02 s9 permits LRFD or ASD). ASD would require 0.7E load effects against allowable capacities; LRFD was chosen because the catalogue and deck tables publish phi factors and the optimisation is on the same basis. Rejected as an alternative format, not as a design.
4. **Isolated panel piers with no joint connectors (JC0)**. Saves $22,715 but removes the panel-to-panel shear transfer on which the intermediate precast wall system depends; the wall lines would act as independent cantilevers and would not qualify as the selected system. Rejected.
5. **Section 12.10.3 or 12.10.4 diaphragm design** (FEMA P-2082-1 options). SDC-02 s5 expressly does not use them. Rejected.
6. **WA2 or WA3 wall anchors at wider spacing**. Feasible but costlier than WA1 at 8 ft ($14,448 or $18,300 against $10,176). Rejected on cost.
7. **Wind as the governing lateral load**. WM-2026-09 reports 184 kips N-S and 138 kips E-W strength-level, below the seismic base shear of 312 kips. Rejected.
8. **Site Class C / Parcel 4B motions** (GEO-2019-118). The report is for the adjacent parcel under ASCE 7-16 and SDC-02 s3 and GEO-2026-071 both state it does not apply. Rejected.

## 10. Deflection and drift

Semi-rigid diaphragm deflection plus wall-line drift, amplified by Cd/Ie = 3.2: worst case 2.78 in at the future-mass 100/30 case, against the Engineer of Record's permissible 4.0 in (SDC-02 s7; ASCE 7-22 s12.12.2). Wall-line drift alone, amplified, is 0.23 in against the allowable storey drift of 0.020 h = 6.72 in for Risk Category III 'all other structures' (ASCE 7-22 Table 12.12-1).

Out-of-plane anchorage follows ASCE 7-22 s12.11.2.1 with the flexible-diaphragm amplification ka. The span Lf of the flexible diaphragm is the distance between the wall lines that resist the out-of-plane force: 180 ft for the S and N walls and 240 ft for the W and E walls (UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1). ka = 1.0 + (Lf/100)^2 = 4.24 and 6.76, capped at 2.0, so ka = 2.0 on every wall.

Wp per foot of wall is the lever-action tributary weight of the panel: 1,716 plf (FEMA P-2192-V1 s7.6.1 Step 1 form; SDC-02 s6). The anchorage force is

Fp = 0.4 SDS ka Ie Wp = 0.4 x 0.44 x 2.0 x 1.25 x 1,716 = 755 plf.

Anchors are RPC WA1 joist-seat anchors (Tn = 9.4 kip, phi = 0.75, capacity 7.05 kip) at 8 ft spacing: demand 755 x 8 / 1,000 = 6.04 kip, utilization 0.86. The 4 ft, 6 ft, 8 ft and 10 ft spacings available in the catalogue were priced; WA1 at 10 ft fails (7.55 kip > 7.05 kip), WA2 at 10 ft passes but costs $14,448 against $10,080 for WA1 at 8 ft, and WA3 is more expensive again, so WA1 at 8 ft is the cheapest feasible anchorage.

Continuous ties are provided by the joists at 6 ft centres (S-201 Rev 2 note 4) and by the continuous chord/collector member on each wall line. The subdiaphragm is the 6 ft deep deck strip between the wall and the first joist tie with an 8 ft span between anchors: L/d = 8/6 = 1.33 <= 2.5 (ASCE 7-22 s12.11.2.2.1 as invoked by SDC-02 s6).

# Building B — seismic diaphragm shears and shear wall loads

You are the delegated design engineer for the lateral load path of **Building B** at the
Continental Divide Data Center in Lewis and Clark County, Montana. The shell is erected: the
precast wall panels are up, the roof deck is laid, and the Engineer of Record has issued the
project documents to you in `project/`, with the published standards available on this project in
`library/`.

Building B is a one-storey box. The exterior walls are 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete
panels that span vertically from the foundation to the roof and cantilever above it to the top of
the parapet; they are the only seismic force-resisting elements. The roof is a bare steel deck
diaphragm on open-web joists, pierced by a mechanical well and a skylight band, and it carries six
roof-top units.

**The Engineer of Record has not selected the precast shear wall system, the deck attachment, the
chords and collectors, the panel connections or the anchorage. That is your scope.** Design it,
analyse it, and hand over the package below.

## What you are asked to produce

Write these five files, then zip them (no enclosing folder) to `output/submission.zip`:

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `design_record.json` | the machine-readable design and the quantities you report |
| `diaphragm_plan.dxf` | the plan drawings for the delegated design engineer |
| `seismic_calculations.xlsx` | the calculation package |
| `constraint_register.xlsx` | the requirements you applied, with their sources |
| `design_basis.md` | the design basis narrative |

Templates for all five, with the exact keys, sheet names and layer names, are in `templates/`.
Start from them. **Write a first complete version of all five files early — within roughly your
first 100 steps — and improve it afterwards; a package that is never written scores zero.**

### `diaphragm_plan.dxf`

Two plan views of the roof, one for **E-W** loading and one for **N-S** loading, in feet, showing
for each direction:

* the **seismic roof diaphragm shear** — the distributed diaphragm force `w_px` in **plf** along
  the building, and the design unit shear in each deck attachment zone;
* the **applied shear wall load `F_x` in kips** on each of the four exterior wall lines;
* the chord, collector and drag strut runs with their design axial forces;
* the deck attachment zone boundaries with the pattern assigned to each zone;
* a revision block, and a statement of whether the package is ASD or LRFD.

Required layers: `DIAPHRAGM_SHEAR`, `WALL_FORCE`, `CHORD`, `COLLECTOR`, `DECK_ZONE`, `GRID`,
`TITLE`.

### `seismic_calculations.xlsx`

Sheets `WEIGHTS`, `BASE_SHEAR`, `DIAPHRAGM_FORCES`, `WALL_FORCES`, `PARAPET_ANCHORAGE`,
`CHORD_FORCES`, covering the effective seismic weight, the seismic response coefficient, the
vertical distribution, the diaphragm design forces, the transfer of the inertia of the wall
cantilevering above the deck, the chord forces, and the force on every wall line for every design
case the criteria list.

### `constraint_register.xlsx`

One row per requirement you applied: the **document**, the **clause, table or section**, the
**value**, and the **items it binds**. It is scored on how many of the governing requirements you
found and cited, and on whether you cited them correctly — rows whose source is a superseded
document, another building or another load case count against you, while extra correct rows do
not. A register that reaches fewer than **60 %** of the governing requirements loses that credit
entirely. A hard requirement you never registered is treated as one you never applied.

### `design_basis.md`

State, with the clause you relied on: the seismic force-resisting system you selected and why it
is the cost-efficient choice; how you resolved every conflict you found between the documents;
the governing check on each wall line; the alternatives you rejected; and the installed cost of
your scope against the budget.

## How your design is judged

Your design is re-analysed by the project's own protocol and checked against every requirement in
the project documents, on design cases you are not shown as well as the ones you are. Within the
requirements, the cheaper installed cost of the lateral scope wins: the score rewards a design
that satisfies everything at the lowest cost, and a design that violates a safety or capacity
requirement keeps none of its cost credit. Each design case scores 0.4·p + 0.6·[h = 1]·O, where p
is the fraction of the 34 constraint families that count, h the fraction of the 21 hard families
that count (a family counts when the design satisfies it and every hard requirement that governs it
is in your register; [h = 1] is 1 when all 21 count, else 0), and O is a certified lower bound on
the installed cost divided by your installed cost, at most 1. The score is the mean over the design
cases.

Units are feet, kips and plf unless a document says otherwise. Where the documents disagree, find
the reading the project record supports and say which you took.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

                      Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT     SDC-02                                REVISION     2      DATE          2026-08-14

TITLE        STRUCTURAL DESIGN CRITERIA                                ISSUED BY     Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC




1. GOVERNING CODES AND STANDARDS
The governing building code is the 2024 IBC as adopted by the State of Montana (ARM 24.301.131). Structural loads,
load combinations and seismic design requirements are those of ASCE/SEI 7-22. Concrete design is to ACI 318-19.
Steel deck diaphragms are to AISI S310. The authority having jurisdiction is the Lewis and Clark County Building
Division, Montana.
A reference copy of the design coefficients and factors for basic seismic force-resisting systems is carried in the
project library (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1, a replacement for ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.2-1 with the same coefficients for
the precast concrete shear wall rows). The library also carries FEMA P-2192-V1 Chapter 7, Horizontal Diaphragm
Design, and the 2020 NEHRP Provisions Chapter 12 modifications. Design to the ASCE/SEI 7-22 clauses; the library
documents are the reference copies available on this project.

2. RISK CATEGORY AND IMPORTANCE FACTOR
Building B is assigned Risk Category III. The assignment follows the Owner's Basis of Design (OBD-CDDC-B):
Building B houses the county 911 emergency communications tenant on the east side of the data hall, which is an
occupancy required for emergency response. The seismic importance factor is therefore Ie = 1.25 (ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 11.5.1, Table 1.5-2). The code-analysis block on the architectural cover sheet still shows Risk Category II
from the schematic issue and is superseded by this document.

3. SEISMIC GROUND MOTION AND SITE CLASS
The site is at latitude 46.6832, longitude -111.9756 in Lewis and Clark County Building Division, Montana. The site
class is Site Class D from the measured shear wave velocity profile in GEO-2026-071 for this parcel. The 2019 report
GEO-2019-118 covers the adjacent Parcel 4B, is based on ASCE/SEI 7-16, and does not apply to Building B.

Design spectral response acceleration parameters are taken from the USGS Seismic Design Web Service output
held in this folder for the governing standard, risk category and site class. The seismic design category is determined
from ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 11.6 using both SDS and SD1; the more severe governs.

4. SEISMIC FORCE-RESISTING SYSTEM
The seismic force-resisting system is the perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast concrete wall panels acting as
bearing-wall shear walls. There are no interior shear walls or braced frames. The Engineer of Record has NOT
selected the precast shear wall category: the delegated designer shall select the most cost-efficient system permitted
for the seismic design category and structural height, balancing the detailing and connection-qualification
requirements against the response modification coefficient, and shall state the selection with its R, Ω0 and Cd and the
clause that permits it.

Where the tabulated overstrength factor is 2.5 or greater it may be reduced by 0.5 for structures with flexible
diaphragms (footnote b to the table). Building B's roof is a bare (untopped) steel deck diaphragm on concrete shear
walls and is a flexible-diaphragm structure under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1.

5. DIAPHRAGM DESIGN
 The roof diaphragm is a bare steel deck diaphragm and is designed by the traditional provisions of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2. The alternative provisions of Section 12.10.3 are not used on this project, and Section
12.10.4 is not used because the Owner's serviceability criterion in Section 7 below governs the diaphragm stiffness.
Note that the Section 12.10 Exception that bars Sections 12.10.1 and 12.10.2 applies to precast concrete
diaphragms; the Building B roof diaphragm is steel deck, not precast.

Collectors, drag struts and their connections to the vertical elements are designed for the amplified force required for
this seismic design category. Continuous chords are required on all four diaphragm edges and on all four sides of
every roof opening. A continuous drag strut is required across every wall opening 12 ft wide or wider so that
diaphragm shear is delivered to the full-height piers.

6. STRUCTURAL WALLS AND THEIR ANCHORAGE
Anchorage of the precast wall panels to the roof diaphragm is designed to ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.11.2.1,
including the amplification ka for flexible diaphragms. The span of the flexible diaphragm Lf is determined as shown in
UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1 (library). Continuous ties are required across the diaphragm; subdiaphragms used to
transfer the anchorage force to the continuous ties shall not exceed the length-to-depth ratio of ASCE/SEI 7-22
Section 12.11.2.2.1.

The panels span vertically from the foundation to the roof diaphragm and cantilever above it to the top of the parapet.
The weight tributary to the roof, and the anchorage force, shall account for the lever action of that cantilever; see the
worked one-storey bare-deck example in FEMA P-2192-V1 Section 7.6.1 Step 1 for the form of the tributary
calculation.

7. DRIFT AND DEFLECTION CRITERIA
Storey drift is limited to the allowable storey drift of ASCE/SEI 7-22 Table 12.12-1 for this risk category ('all other
structures'), applied to the design storey drift of Section 12.8.6.
Diaphragm deflection. Under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.12.2 the deflection in the plane of the diaphragm shall not
exceed the permissible deflection of the attached elements. For Building B the attached elements are the precast wall
panels, whose out-of-plane stability governs. The Engineer of Record's permissible value is 4.0 in (approximately
h/84 for the 28 ft panel, from the out-of-plane slender-wall stability check of the panel under the design earthquake
displacement), applied to the design (amplified) deflection Cdδ/Ie of the top of the panel, that is the diaphragm
deflection plus the drift of the wall line supporting it.
 8. LOAD CASES TO BE REPORTED
Accidental torsion is applied as required by ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.8.4.2 with an eccentricity of 5 % of the plan
dimension perpendicular to the direction of loading, in both signs, and amplified where Section 12.8.4.3 requires it. In
addition to the two orthogonal directions, the Owner requires the 100 % / 30 % orthogonal combination to be reported
for the cases listed below. The construction-stage cases are the erector's temporary condition and use the reduced
construction-period seismic load of ERC-07.
CASE      DIRECTION     ACCIDENTAL ECCENTRICITY      MASS CASE      ORTHOGONAL       STAGE

S01       X             +1                           base           -                final

S02       X             -1                           base           -                final

S03       Y             +1                           base           -                final

S04       Y             -1                           base           -                final

S05       X             +1                           base           100/30           final

S06       Y             -1                           base           100/30           final

S07       X             +1                           future         -                final

S08       Y             +1                           future         -                final

S09       X             -1                           future         100/30           final

S10       Y             -1                           future         100/30           final

S11       X             +1                           erection       -                erection

S12       Y             -1                           erection       -                erection

The 'future' mass case includes the two phase-2 roof-top units reserved in the Owner's Basis of Design. The
delegated design shall be adequate for every case.

9. DESIGN FORMAT
The delegated designer may work in LRFD or in ASD. Every load and every capacity presented in the deliverable
shall be clearly identified as ASD or as LRFD, and the format shall be used consistently throughout the
package. Where an ASD package is presented, seismic load effects are 0.7E and capacities are the allowable values
of the referenced material standard.

10. ANALYSIS
The structural peer reviewer requires the diaphragm force distribution to be the envelope of flexible, rigid and
semi-rigid behaviour; see PR-07. The analysis shall follow the project protocol DAP-2, which defines the model, the
properties, the application of the accidental torsion and the reduction of the computed field to design values. A
verification example is published in DAP-2 Appendix A.

11. DELEGATED DESIGN SCOPE AND BUDGET
The lateral scope covered by this delegated design is the deck attachment, the chords, collectors and drag struts, the
panel joint connectors, the panel base tie-downs, the wall-to-diaphragm anchorage and the seismic force-resisting
system detailing premium. Unit rates and the capital cap for that scope are in PROC-114. The installed cost of the
lateral scope shall not exceed the cap.

                           Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT         DAP-2                                      REVISION   1   DATE        2026-07-31

TITLE            DIAPHRAGM ANALYSIS PROTOCOL                               ISSUED BY   Torrey Ridge Structural Engineers PLLC




1. PURPOSE
This protocol defines the analysis every delegated lateral design for Building B is checked against. It fixes the model,
the member properties, the load application and the reduction of the computed field to design values, so that two
engineers analysing the same design obtain the same design quantities. Designs are verified against this protocol; a
design whose own analysis differs from it will be assessed on the protocol's results.

2. THE TWO STAGES
Stage A is the in-plane model of a wall segment - a continuous run of precast panels between openings. Stage B is
the in-plane model of the roof diaphragm, supported on springs whose stiffnesses come from Stage A.

3. STAGE A - JOINTED PRECAST WALL SEGMENT
Each panel in a segment is a cantilever fixed at the foundation and free at the top, with three degrees of freedom at its
top: lateral displacement u, vertical displacement v and rotation θ. The cantilever height is the height to the roof
diaphragm (the parapet above the diaphragm is not part of the in-plane cantilever). Flexural and shear flexibility are
both included:
  fuu = h³/(3EI) + h/(GAv), fuθ = h²/(2EI), fθθ = h/EI,   kvv = EA/h

with Ec = 57,000√f'c psi for f'c = 6000 psi, Gc = Ec/2.4, Av = 5/6 of the gross area, and I taken as 0.50 Ig (cracked, ACI
318-19 Table 6.6.3.1.1(a)). The axial stiffness uses the gross area. A segment interrupted over part of its height by an
opening that does not reach the foundation (a spandrel) keeps its length, and its flexural and shear rigidities are
factored by the solid fraction of the height.

Adjacent panels are connected by the vertical shear spring formed by their joint connectors: the spring stiffness is the
number of connectors in the joint times the connector stiffness of the manufacturer's table, and it acts on the relative
vertical slip of the two panel edges,
  slip = (vi + θi Li/2) − (vi+1 − θi+1 Li+1/2).

The roof chord ties the tops of the panels of one segment to a common lateral displacement. Condensing the
segment on that displacement gives the segment lateral stiffness kseg; recovering the internal state for a unit segment
force gives the shear in every joint and, for every panel, its base moment and its axial force. A panel's tie-down
carries its own base couple, taken on an internal lever arm of 0.8 times the panel length, plus the coupling axial force
delivered to it.

4. STAGE B - ROOF DIAPHRAGM
The roof is modelled as a plane-stress membrane mesh on a 10 ft square grid, with the elements whose centroid falls
inside a roof opening removed. The constitutive matrix is written directly in force-per-unit-length terms:
  D = diag(A′, A′, G′)

where G′ is the diaphragm shear stiffness of the attachment pattern assigned to the zone the element lies in, from the
manufacturer's diaphragm table, and A′ = 1740 kip/in is the smeared in-plane axial rigidity of the bare deck sheet
(29,000 ksi on 0.72 in² per foot of width). Poisson's ratio is taken as zero. Integration is 2 x 2 Gauss.
 Chords, collectors and drag struts are two-node bar elements on the lines they are placed on, with EA from the
member's area and E = 29,000 ksi. Every wall segment is a spring to ground acting in the plane of its own wall line,
distributed over the mesh nodes the segment spans in proportion to the length each node carries. The wall lines
perpendicular to the direction of loading are part of the model: they are what resists the plan rotation of the
diaphragm.

5. LOADS
The inertial force applied to the diaphragm is the diaphragm design force coefficient times the mass tributary to the
diaphragm: the roof dead load over the net deck area, the roof-top units at their own positions, and the tributary
weight of the wall lines perpendicular to the direction of loading. The wall lines parallel to the direction of loading carry
their own inertia directly into their own springs and are not part of the diaphragm force.
Accidental torsion is applied as a plan moment about the centre of mass equal to 5 % of the plan dimension
perpendicular to the loading times the total applied force, distributed over the mesh as a mass-proportional rotational
force field. The torsional amplification factor Ax is computed from the maximum and average displacements of the wall
lines resisting the direction of loading, using the rigid model, and is capped at 3.0.

6. REDUCTION TO DESIGN VALUES
6.1 Zone design shear. The design unit shear of an attachment zone is the largest SECTION mean in that zone: for
every mesh line crossing the zone, the mean of the absolute element shear flows of the elements of that line inside
the zone is formed, and the zone value is the largest of those means over both mesh directions. A single element at a
re-entrant corner is a stress concentration and is not a design shear.
6.2 Deflections and drift are taken from the semi-rigid model, with the real stiffness of the design. Forces are taken
from the envelope of Section 6.3.
6.3 Envelope. Every design force - zone shear, wall line force, wall segment force, chord and collector axial force - is
the largest of the three idealisations:
  flexible: the diaphragm is a simple beam spanning between the two wall lines that resist the direction of loading; the unit shear at a
section is the beam shear divided by the net diaphragm depth at that section, and the chord force is the beam moment divided by the
same depth. Accidental torsion is not transferred in the flexible idealisation.

  rigid: the Stage B model with the membrane rigidities multiplied by 107.

  semi-rigid: the Stage B model as built.

6.4 Orthogonal cases. For the cases the design criteria mark 100/30, the demands are those of the case direction
plus 0.30 times the demands of the companion case in the orthogonal direction with the same mass case, same sign
of accidental eccentricity and same stage.
 APPENDIX A - VERIFICATION EXAMPLE VP-1
An implementation of this protocol that reproduces the following Stage A result is consistent with the reference
implementation. No other verification values are published.

Case. A single wall segment 40.0 ft long, on a wall line with no openings within the segment, built from four 10.0 ft
panels, 8 in solid normal-weight precast, cantilever height 28.0 ft to the diaphragm, f'c = 6,000 psi, cracked flexural
rigidity per Section 3, joints connected by three RPC-40 connectors each (joint spring 3 x 320 = 960 kip/in).
QUANTITY                                                                             VALUE

segment lateral stiffness k_seg                                                      1,279.4 kip/in

shear in joint 1 (end joint), per kip of segment force                               0.2630 kip/kip

shear in joint 2 (middle joint), per kip of segment force                            0.2527 kip/kip

base moment of panel 1, per kip of segment force                                     88.91 kip-in/kip

axial force in panel 1, per kip of segment force                                     0.2630 kip/kip

The same segment with no joint connectors (isolated panel piers) has kseg = 769.2 kip/in.
 =====PR07=====
                      Continental Divide Data Center - Building B
DOCUMENT      PR-07                                  REVISION     -       DATE          2026-08-03

TITLE         STRUCTURAL PEER REVIEW - COMMENT AND RESOLUTION             ISSUED BY     Gallatin Peer Review Group LLC



To: Engineer of Record. Subject: Building B lateral system, review comment 7.

COMMENT 7

The roof diaphragm of Building B may be idealised as flexible under ASCE/SEI 7-22 Section 12.3.1.1 because the
vertical elements are concrete shear walls and the deck is untopped steel. The reviewer does not accept a flexible
idealisation as the sole basis of design for this building. The roof is pierced by a 60 ft x 40 ft mechanical well and an
80 ft x 20 ft skylight band, the wall lines are very unequally pierced by openings - the west wall has a single 40 ft
electrical yard opening and the south wall has five dock doors - and the erected panel positions differ from the record
set. The centre of rigidity is therefore not at the centre of the plan and a tributary-width distribution does not bound the
wall line forces.

REQUIREMENT

The design forces for the diaphragm, the collectors and the wall lines shall be the envelope of the flexible, rigid and
semi-rigid distributions, each computed by the project protocol DAP-2. The semi-rigid model shall use the erected
geometry, not the record geometry. Deflections shall be reported from the semi-rigid model.

RESOLUTION

Accepted by the Engineer of Record and incorporated in SDC-02 Rev 2 Section 10 and in protocol DAP-2. Closed.

1.4 Tenancy and occupancy
Building B houses the primary data hall and, on its east side, the Lewis and Clark County consolidated 911 emergency communications tenant, including the dispatch floor and the radio equipment room. The Owner requires that the roof diaphragm be stiff enough that the precast wall panels it braces remain stable out of plane under the design earthquake, and that no permanent deformation of the roof membrane occurs. 5.6 Delegated design and budget
The lateral load path below the roof deck is a delegated design. The delegated designer selects the precast shear wall system, the deck attachment, the chords, collectors and drag struts, the panel connections and the anchorage. exit_code=0
# Building B - seismic diaphragm and shear wall design basis

Design format: **LRFD** (every load and resistance in this package is strength-level; capacities use phi factors: deck phi = 0.60 per AISI S310, connectors, tie-downs and anchors phi = 0.75, steel members phi = 0.90).

Project: Continental Divide Data Center - Building B, Lewis and Clark County, Montana. Delegated lateral design to SDC-02 Rev 2 (2026-08-14), protocol DAP-2 Rev 1 and peer review comment PR-07.

## 1. Seismic basis

Governing code: 2024 IBC as adopted by Montana (ARM 24.301.131); loads and seismic design to ASCE/SEI 7-22; concrete to ACI 318-19; steel deck diaphragms to AISI S310 (SDC-02 s1).

| Parameter | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Risk category | III | OBD-CDDC-B Rev 4 s1.4; SDC-02 s2 (the RC II block on the A-101 cover is superseded) |
| Importance factor Ie | 1.25 | SDC-02 s2; ASCE 7-22 s11.5.1, Table 1.5-2 |
| Site class | D (Vs,100 = 905 ft/s) | GEO-2026-071 s4; SDC-02 s3 |
| S_DS / S_D1 | 0.44 / 0.24 | USGS ASCE7-22, Risk Category III, Site Class D (SDC-02 s3) |
| Seismic Design Category | D (both S_DS and S_D1) | SDC-02 s3; ASCE 7-22 s11.6 |
| Response modification R | 4 (intermediate precast shear walls) | UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 row A.6 |
| Overstrength Omega_0 | 2.5 tabulated; 2.0 applied to collectors | UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 footnote b; SDC-02 s4 |
| Deflection amplification Cd | 4 | UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 row A.6 |
| Period T | 0.243 s = 0.020 (28)^0.75 | ASCE 7-22 Eq. 12.8-7, Table 12.8-2 (all other systems) |
| Seismic response coefficient Cs | 0.1375 = 0.44/(4/1.25) | ASCE 7-22 Eq. 12.8-2; SD1/(T R/Ie) = 0.309 does not govern |
| Effective seismic weight W | 2,270.5 kips | Table WEIGHTS |
| Base shear V | 312.2 kips | ASCE 7-22 Eq. 12.8-1 |

The seismic weight includes the roof dead load of 20 psf over the 39,200 sq ft net deck area (784.0 kips), the six phase-1 roof-top units totalling 45 kips at their M-601 Rev 3 positions, and the wall weight tributary to the roof. The wall tributary weight follows the worked one-storey bare-deck example of FEMA P-2192-V1 s7.6.1 Step 1, as SDC-02 s6 directs: w = 100 psf x 31^2/(2 x 28) = 1,716 plf per foot of wall line. That is a tributary height of 17.16 ft per foot of wall (the 31 ft panel cantilevers from the foundation, is propped at the 28 ft deck and cantilevers a further 3 ft to the parapet). The phase-2 units (2 x 8 kips) are a load case only and raise W to 2,286.5 kips.

## 2. Seismic force-resisting system

**Selected system: intermediate precast concrete shear walls (UFC 3-301-01 Table 3-1 row A.6, detailing reference ACI 318-19 18.2.1.6 / 1905.3), R = 4, Omega_0 = 2.5 (reduced to 2.0 for the flexible diaphragm per footnote b), Cd = 4.**

The system is permitted in Seismic Design Category D up to a structural height of 40 ft (Table 3-1 row A.6, footnote i). Building B is one storey with a structural height hn = 28 ft to the roof (31 ft to the top of parapet), so the 40 ft limit is satisfied with 12 ft to spare. The perimeter 8 in solid normal-weight precast panels are the only seismic force-resisting elements (S-201 Rev 2 note 5; SDC-02 s4).

Cost efficiency: the permitted alternatives are (a) special reinforced concrete shear walls, R = 5 (Table 3-1 row A.1), which would require the ACI ITG-5.2 ductile connector JC3 at $1,240 each (only the RPC-60D is qualified for special precast, RPC catalogue s2) and the special_precast detailing premium of $4,120 per panel, and (b) ordinary precast shear walls, R = 3 (row A.7), which are **NP - not permitted** in SDC D. The R = 5 system reduces the base shear by 20 % (Cs = 0.110 against 0.1375) but adds $183,870 in premiums and about $124,000 in JC3 connector cost, against a deck-attachment saving of under $20,000; it is not cost-effective and is not used. Ordinary precast is not permitted. Intermediate precast with JC1 connectors is the cheapest system that the table permits at this height and SDC.

## 3. As-built geometry

The documents disagree in the following places. Each is resolved to the reading the record supports; the erected geometry governs (RFI-041 closed response; A-101 Rev 3 note 6; SDC-02 s10 and PR-07 require the semi-rigid model to use erected geometry).

## 4. Analysis

The analysis follows DAP-2 exactly. Stage A models each wall segment as a run of precast panels, each a cantilever fixed at the foundation with three top degrees of freedom (u, v, theta) and flexibilities fuu = h^3/(3EI) + h/(G Av), fu-theta = h^2/(2EI), f-theta-theta = h/EI, with Ec = 57,000 sqrt(6000) psi = 4,415 ksi, Gc = Ec/2.4, Av = 5/6 of the gross area and I = 0.50 Ig (DAP-2 s3). Adjacent panels are joined by the vertical shear spring n x k of the RPC connector. Spandrel segments (louvre L-1, L-2 and the EY-1 yard opening) keep their length and have EI and G Av reduced by the solid fraction of the height (21/31 = 0.677 for a 10 ft louvre, 11/31 = 0.355 for the 20 ft EY-1 opening). My implementation reproduces DAP-2 Appendix A VP-1 exactly: kseg = 1,279.4 kip/in, joint shears 0.2630 and 0.2527 kip/kip, panel 1 base moment 88.91 kip-in/kip, axial 0.2630 kip/kip, and 769.2 kip/in with no connectors.

Stage B is a plane-stress membrane on the 10 ft x 10 ft grid (24 x 18 elements) with elements whose centroid falls inside RO-1 (60 x 40 ft) or RO-2 (80 x 20 ft) removed, D = diag(1740, 1740, G') kip/in, zero Poisson ratio and 2 x 2 Gauss integration (DAP-2 s4). Each wall segment is a spring to ground in the plane of its own wall line, distributed over the nodes it spans in proportion to the length each node carries. Chords are two-node bars with E = 29,000 ksi. Every case is run three times: flexible (simple beam), rigid (membrane rigidities x 10^7) and semi-rigid (as built). Design forces are the envelope (DAP-2 s6.3; PR-07), with the 100/30 orthogonal combination of DAP-2 s6.4 applied to cases S05, S06, S09 and S10.

The rigid model gives Ax = 1.00 for every case (the maximum wall-line displacement does not exceed 1.2 times the average), so no torsional amplification is applied; the accidental eccentricity is 5 % of the plan dimension in both signs.

Units: feet, kips and plf; displacements in inches.

## 6. Wall anchorage and the parapet cantilever

Out-of-plane anchorage follows ASCE 7-22 s12.11.2.1 with the flexible-diaphragm amplification ka. The span Lf of the flexible diaphragm is the distance between the wall lines that resist the out-of-plane force: 180 ft for the S and N walls and 240 ft for the W and E walls (UFC 3-301-01 Figure 3-1). ka = 1.0 + (Lf/100)^2 = 4.24 and 6.76, capped at 2.0, so ka = 2.0 on every wall.

Wp per foot of wall is the lever-action tributary weight of the panel: 1,716 plf (FEMA P-2192-V1 s7.6.1 Step 1 form; SDC-02 s6). The anchorage force is

Fp = 0.4 SDS ka Ie Wp = 0.4 x 0.44 x 2.0 x 1.25 x 1,716 = 755 plf.

Anchors are RPC WA1 joist-seat anchors (Tn = 9.4 kip, phi = 0.75, capacity 7.05 kip) at 8 ft spacing: demand 755 x 8 / 1,000 = 6.04 kip, utilization 0.86. The 4 ft, 6 ft, 8 ft and 10 ft spacings available in the catalogue were priced; WA1 at 10 ft fails (7.55 kip > 7.05 kip), WA2 at 10 ft passes but costs $14,448 against $10,080 for WA1 at 8 ft, and WA3 is more expensive again, so WA1 at 8 ft is the cheapest feasible anchorage.

Continuous ties are provided by the joists at 6 ft centres (S-201 Rev 2 note 4) and by the continuous chord/collector member on each wall line. The subdiaphragm is the 6 ft deep deck strip between the wall and the first joist tie with an 8 ft span between anchors: L/d = 8/6 = 1.33 <= 2.5 (ASCE 7-22 s12.11.2.2.1 as invoked by SDC-02 s6).

The panel joints use one RPC-24 (JC1) per vertical joint, the catalogue connector qualified for intermediate precast shear walls (RPC-CAT-2026 Rev 3 s2). Base tie-downs are BA2 (4-#8 dowel plus grouted sleeve, Tn = 88 kip, phi Tn = 66 kip), one per erected panel; the capacities are the connection capacities of the catalogue. The resistance of the footing to the tie-down (footing dead weight plus 0.45 times the vertical effective stress on the keyway, GEO-2026-071 s9) is by the Engineer of Record and is outside this delegated scope. The governing tie-down is the end panel of the 16 ft S pier at x = 32 ft (60.1 kip); the end panels of the long N, W and E piers carry 34.6, 44.1 and 42.8 kip.
